title: Angular leaf spot on common bean

Header: Angular leaf spot on common bean

Prevention: Plant resistant bean cultivars such as
Plant pathogen free seed to ensure disease free seedlings
Treat seed with fungicides such as
Remove or bury infected plant debris or residue and volunteer plants before planting in a garden
Practice a minimum of 2 year crop rotation with a non-host crops such as cereals and root crops
Avoid movement in the bean fields when the plants are wet, since this moves spores from one plant to another
Monitoring: Monitor fields regularly throughout the season.
Look out for symptoms which first appear on the primary leaves, becoming clearer at late flowering.
Symptoms/lesions on leaves, petioles and pods are angular (limited by the veins) and grey, and those on the lower leaf surfaces may have black spores that look like minute spines.
Direct Control: Remove crop debris or deep plough the crop debris or residues to depth of 1.2 metres
Minimise water splashes by sprinkler irrigation to avoid spread of spores
Restrictions: Ia = Extremely hazardous; Ib = Highly hazardous; II = Moderately hazardous; III = slightly hazardous; U = Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use; FM = Fumigant, not classified
O = Obsolete as pesticide, not classified.
Please follow insecticide manufacturer’s instructions on application rate, a method of application and mixing.
Always check for the expiry date and wear protective clothing
Apply fungicides to reduce the disease build up, with the first spray at 3 weeks after planting, second at 50% flowering and third at podding.
Or apply as soon as you see the first symptoms and do exceed 3 sprays within the season.
Use the dosage recommended by the manufacturer.
